summary: Climate Skin is a passive roofing system designed to explore ways of reducing heat absorption in buildings. Our project compares four different surface models: a conventional flat surface, a reflective surface, a textured surface, and a multi-layer design combining a reflective layer, a textured layer, and an air gap. Our hypothesis is that combining these layers may slow down temperature increase compared to a conventional surface. We aim to test this under the same conditions and investigate a sustainable solution that does not require electricity.
details:
Climate Skin is a passive roofing concept designed to reduce heat absorption in buildings. Our project compares four different surface models to investigate how reflective materials, surface texture, and air gaps affect temperature changes.

Our hypothesis is that combining these layers may slow down temperature increase compared to a conventional surface. We aim to test this under the same conditions.

The project focuses on sustainability, energy efficiency, and passive cooling without electricity. We considered material properties, sunlight reflection, and temperature changes. AI-supported tools were used to create some visuals and assist with simulations.

Our goal is to explore a creative and sustainable roofing solution for the future.
